method_text:
KB-IDEA-EVALUATION-001 v0.1 — Evaluating an Idea
Candidate v0.1 — founder acceptance pending; review state in companion review records

Scope and limits
This A0 proposed method organizes investigation and learning, not a trading engine, acceptance decision or automatic archetype change. It establishes no new current app fields, universal thresholds or feature availability. Evidence sources explain definitions and evaluation risks, not strategy profitability. Use SOURCE-REGISTER.txt for inspected passages and limitations. RECORD-LINKS-AND-APP-HANDOFF.txt is the adjacent companion owned by Astra, not a source the original researcher inspected; authoritative IDs and schemas remain to be mapped.

Meanings, not compulsory screens
An observation records what was seen, with source, time and coverage. An idea proposes an interpretation or improvement. An investigation asks a bounded question and obtains relevant evidence. A trial deliberately evaluates a frozen alternative under stated constraints. A supported lesson is a conclusion justified within its evidence boundary; an adopted change is a separate authorized behavioral decision with scope and effective version. These meanings do not require separate screens or a compulsory trial for every question. Clarifying an ambiguous study may resolve an investigation without any portfolio simulation.

Link the originating observation to subsequent interpretations rather than overwrite it when explanations change. Preserve originating owner and archetype throughout Command Center investigation, including alternatives and later corrections. An investment idea concerns a business, sector or catalyst. A learning idea concerns selection, timing, ranking, execution, risk or partnership behavior and needs no ticker or watchlist. For example, “preserve the cohort in follow-up rankings” is a learning idea even without a security recommendation.

Frame a discriminating question
State the claim, horizon and proposed mechanism precisely enough to distinguish alternatives. Ask what evidence would weaken it before examining outcomes. With C1, “Does proximity to a rising completed-daily average add useful subsequent-return information beyond comparable pullbacks?” is narrower than “NVDA is strong.” Attention near a reference is a mechanism hypothesis, not observed order flow. Broad-market decline, temporary liquidity pressure and prior price structure remain alternatives. M1 and V1 support those distinctions, not a demonstrated edge.

C1's October 30, 2026 noon observation records decline while above a rising daily average and provisional matched-window participation. It supplies no catalyst, aligned market/sector return or later outcome. A proposed Command Center investigation can request those missing comparisons; a battle partner can discuss concentration, timing and existing eligibility; FantasyTimes can describe the dated path with qualifications. These are proposed method consumers, not verified implemented routes. The shared factual observation does not become separate independent evidence each time it is reused.

Freeze a fair comparison
Before testing, preserve baseline and candidate versions, input definitions, allowed actions, objective, benchmark, horizon, risk limits and stopping conditions. These are A0 design requirements, not asserted existing fields. The objective depends on the question: clearer cohort continuity, better calibrated forecasts, lower implementation cost or improved portfolio outcomes require different measurements. Compare against the actual existing approach or another justified benchmark, not only the most convenient losing alternative.

For a pullback question, M1 proposes comparable eligible episodes at observable landmarks and subsequent outcomes excluding the qualifying rebound. Freeze eligibility and classification using information available then. Record every eligible opportunity, observed/excluded case and reason, all tested variants and contrary evidence. Include hold and skip alternatives. Preserve the original ranking cohort under I1/I2 limitations; a candidate discovered only after changing filters belongs to a different comparison. An ineligible entry that later rises remains ineligible under the original rule. It can motivate a new investigation, not a retroactive exception or adoption.

Separate types of evidence
Historical replay reconstructs past alternatives under explicit assumptions; forward simulation records decisions before subsequently observed outcomes; actual game decisions document what was proposed and executed under active constraints. None is interchangeable. I5 shows that a swap rationale can accompany a held or failed action. I6 does not establish replay comparison scope. A synthetic single-swap-versus-hold example cannot establish effects of a complete portfolio policy with later trades.

Do not grant a fill at an already observed pre-decision price. State submission and first eligible execution timing, price source/delay, quantities, cash, holdings, costs, missing/stale-data and corporate-action assumptions. Missing inputs may leave one comparison inconclusive without blocking unrelated interpretation. C1 is retrospective and its proxies are not executions; its feed coverage assumptions and original unknown volume gate remain intact. No new numerical analysis is supplied here; calculations belong in tested tools.

Guard against learning the wrong lesson
Hindsight imports later knowledge; selection highlights favorable cases; survivorship discards names or variants that disappeared. Retain exclusions and unsuccessful variants. Repeated observations from the same episode and related sector exposures are not independent replications. Missingness can select an unusually complete subset. Costs and execution friction can overturn a gross comparison. Record contrary cases instead of explaining them away after seeing outcomes.

E1's inspected abstract/introduction explains how repeated searching can select noise and inflate apparent backtest success. Preserve exploratory work separately from later confirmation with frozen definitions and genuinely later or appropriately reserved evidence. Merely naming a holdout or citing E1 does not implement PBO/CSCV or certify an unoverfit strategy. Observational comparisons remain observational, not causal experiments. No universal trade count establishes validation; adequacy depends on question, coverage, dependence and uncertainty.

Conclusions, adoption and ownership
Describe a conclusion as supported, challenged or inconclusive within its boundary. These descriptions are distinct from job progress, package review/acceptance and behavioral adoption; retain existing app vocabulary wherever defined. Related positions winning in one episode plus a trial showing no clear difference can remain inconclusive. Retaining the baseline or retiring a variant are valid lessons. A profitable outcome alone does not justify a permanent rule.

Start with coverage and uncertainty, not a numerical confidence badge. Numerical confidence requires a defined event and horizon, forecasts recorded before outcomes and suitable calibration evidence. C1 cannot provide that from a single retrospective description.

Archetype identity constrains trials and adoption even when another approach looks attractive. Proposed responsibilities, pending app verification: Practice Field executes forward portfolio trials; Forge manages compatible versioned adoption; Film Room reviews decisions and outcomes. Their existence as complete services is not demonstrated. Adoption requires separate authorization, compatible version, effective scope and rollback reference, not merely a supported conclusion.

General methods may be shared. Private records, derived summaries and learned adjustments stay with the originating user/archetype; validation grants no sharing permission. A0 proposes authenticated owner/archetype checks before retrieval, summary, export and model-context assembly. I4's battle authorization and I6's owner-oriented screen are bounded observations, not proof of end-to-end enforcement. Keep another archetype's private case out of permitted context and shared exports; a model instruction or caller-supplied owner ID is insufficient authorization.
